question: What three types of signs are required at an interchange exit-ramp terminal where wrong-way entry could inadvertently occur?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Based on the illustrated example in Figure 2B-15, the three sign types shown at an exit-ramp termination to deter wrong-way entry are DO NOT ENTER (R5-1) signs, WRONG WAY (R5-1a) signs, and ONE WAY (R6-1) signs (supplemented by STOP or YIELD control for the ramp itself). However, the text evidence provided does not include the actual Standard provision (Section 2B.48) that mandates these signs, so the "shall" requirement cannot be quoted verbatim; the answer here rests on the figure and related supporting/cross-referencing material. Standards (mandatory): - No Standard provision in the supplied text evidence directly states the required signs at an exit-ramp terminal. (The Standards supplied — Section 2J.07 §2 on Specific Service ramp signs and Section 2E.21 §2 on interchange guide signs — address guide signing, not wrong-way deterrence.) Guidance (recommended): - "To minimize wrong-way movements onto freeway or expressway exit ramps, Street Name signs should not be used at the intersection of a freeway or expressway exit ramp with the crossroad to display the name of the freeway or expressway to traffic on the crossroad." (related wrong-way prevention guidance) Options (permitted): - A Directional assembly with a diagonal downward-pointing arrow (M6-2aP) plaque may be used at the far left-hand corner of an intersection with a freeway or expressway entrance ramp, facing left-turning traffic, to indicate the point of entry and "distinguish the entrance ramp from an adjoining exit ramp terminal at the same intersection" — a permitted measure that helps drivers avoid inadvertently entering the exit ramp. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2B-15 depicts the exit-ramp termination with DO NOT ENTER signs, WRONG WAY signs, and ONE WAY signs (plus STOP or YIELD control and wrong-way pavement arrows) positioned to face potential wrong-way entrants. [Image 2] shows the same Figure 2B-15 in its full-page context on page 112, titled "Example of Application of Regulatory Signing and Pavement Markings at an Exit Ramp Termination to Deter Wrong-Way Entry," cross-referenced to Section 2B.48. [Image 3] shows Section 2B.46 and Figure 2B-13, identifying the sign designations DO NOT ENTER (R5-1), WRONG WAY (R5-1a), and ONE WAY (R6-1/R6-2), and stating the R5-1 sign shall be used at "the intersection of an interchange exit ramp with a crossroad as specified in Section 2B.48." [Image 4] is the table of figures listing Figure 2B-15's title on page 112. [Image 5] shows Figure 2D-18, whose note 3 directs readers to "Section 2B.48 and Figure 2B-15 for an example of regulatory signing and pavement markings at an exit ramp termination to deter wrong-way entry." Citations: - Figure 2B-15 (p.112) - Page 150 - Page 153 - Page 29 - Page 297 - Section 2D.45 Guidance §3 (p.247) - Section 2D.50 Option §3 (p.254)
gold_answer: At least one ONE WAY sign for each crossroad travel direction, at least one DO NOT ENTER sign near the downstream end of the exit ramp, and at least one WRONG WAY sign on the exit ramp facing wrong-way road users are required.
